events.headline: First Solar reports Q1 2022 net loss of $0.41/share on $367M sales; reiterates full-year 2022 guidance
events.detail: Q1 2022 net sales were $367 million with a net loss of $0.41 per diluted share, down from Q4 2021's $1.23 EPS. The company reiterated its full-year 2022 guidance of $2.4-$2.6 billion net sales and $0.00-$0.60 diluted EPS unchanged.

source.title: First Solar, Inc. Announces First Quarter 2022 Financial Results (8-K Ex. 99.1)

events.headline: Inflation Reduction Act signed into law, creating a Section 45X production credit for US-made solar components
events.detail: The Act created a per-component manufacturing production tax credit covering solar cells, wafers, polysilicon and modules made in the United States, with full value through 2029 and phase-down through 2032.

source.title: First Solar to Invest up to $1.2 Billion in Scaling Production of American-Made Responsible Solar by 4.4 GW

events.opened_note: Direct government sources for the Aug 16, 2022 signing date (congress.gov, energy.gov) returned 403/404 when fetched; the Act's passage and date are corroborated here by First Solar's own Aug 30, 2022 press release, which cites the Act by name and quotes the CEO on its passage.

events.headline: First Solar announces up to $1.2 billion of new US capacity, citing the Inflation Reduction Act
events.detail: The company said it would build a new 3.5 GW-DC US Southeast facility (up to $1 billion) and expand Ohio capacity by 0.9 GW-DC ($185 million), targeting over 10 GW-DC of US capacity by 2025 and over 3,000 US manufacturing jobs across four states.
events.source_quote: In passing the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, Congress and the Biden-Harris Administration has entrusted our industry with the responsibility of enabling America's clean energy future.

source.title: First Solar to Invest up to $1.2 Billion in Scaling Production of American-Made Responsible Solar by 4.4 GW

events.headline: First Solar completes sale of a Japan project-development platform to PAG Real Assets
events.detail: First Solar completed the sale of a 293 MW-DC utility-scale solar project development platform in Japan to funds managed by PAG, continuing the planned exit from its Japan legacy business flagged at the cutoff; a related Japan operations-and-maintenance platform sale was still pending at this release.

source.title: First Solar Completes Sale of Japan Project Development Platform to PAG Real Assets

events.opened_note: Player.json's catalyst described the Japan sale as targeted for 'first half of 2022'; this completion, and the pending O&M platform sale referenced in the same release, both fall later than that window.

events.headline: First Solar selects Alabama for a fourth US manufacturing facility, a $1.1 billion, 3.5 GW investment
events.detail: The company said it would build a fully vertically integrated 3.5 GW-DC facility in Lawrence County, Alabama, expected to be commissioned in 2025 and creating over 700 direct jobs, again citing the Inflation Reduction Act.
events.source_quote: The passage of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 has firmly placed America on the path to a sustainable energy future.

source.title: First Solar Selects Alabama for Fourth American Manufacturing Facility

events.headline: US Commerce Department preliminarily finds circumvention of China solar-panel duties via four Southeast Asian countries
events.detail: Commerce issued preliminary affirmative determinations that certain crystalline-silicon panel producers routed Chinese-origin cells/modules through Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand or Vietnam to avoid existing antidumping/countervailing duties, naming specific manufacturers; an existing duty-waiver meant cash deposits were not required on most such imports until June 2024.

source.title: Department of Commerce Issues Preliminary Determination of Circumvention Inquiries of Solar Cells and Modules Produced in China

events.opened_note: Not fetched directly (WebFetch budget prioritized elsewhere); date, agency and substance corroborated by three independent law-firm summaries (Orrick, Norton Rose Fulbright, Foley Hoag) returned in the same search. This case concerns crystalline-silicon competitors, not First Solar's thin-film product directly, but materially affected the competitive/import-cost landscape First Solar's US expansion was designed to exploit.

events.headline: First Solar reports full-year 2022 net loss of $0.41/share, below even the guidance set at the cutoff; guides 2023 EPS to $7.00-$8.00
events.detail: Full-year 2022 net sales were $2.6 billion with a net loss of $0.41 per diluted share (versus FY2021's $4.38 EPS and the $0.00-$0.60 range guided on 2022-03-01), with gross profit of $69.9 million versus $730.0 million in 2021 and $73.1 million of full-year production start-up expense cited. 2023 guidance called for $3.4-$3.6 billion net sales and $7.00-$8.00 diluted EPS.

source.title: First Solar, Inc. Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2022 Financial Results and 2023 Guidance (8-K Ex. 99.1)

events.headline: First Solar's third Ohio manufacturing facility begins Series 7 module production, on the guided H1-2023 schedule
events.detail: The company's FY2023 10-K states production of Series 7 modules commenced at the third Ohio facility 'during 2023'; other company materials place this in the first quarter, consistent with the first-half-2023 timing flagged at the cutoff.
events.source_quote: During 2023, we commenced production of our Series 7 modules at our third manufacturing facility in Ohio.

source.title: First Solar, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2023

events.opened_note: The 10-K does not give an exact calendar date, only 'during 2023'; the 2023-03-31 date used here is an approximation (end of Q1 2023) based on a secondary search summary placing commencement in the quarter ended March 31, 2023, which could not be independently confirmed by opening the Q1 2023 10-Q's operational discussion (only financial-statement text was retrievable via fetch).

events.headline: First Solar inaugurates its first India facility, a 3.3 GW plant in Tamil Nadu, several months after the guided H2-2023 target
events.detail: The $700 million facility, including $500 million of US DFC financing, is First Solar's first fully vertically integrated India plant and sixth operating factory overall, producing Series 7 modules.

source.title: First Solar Inaugurates 3.3 GW Manufacturing Facility in India

events.opened_note: The India facility catalyst flagged at the cutoff targeted second-half 2023; this inauguration in January 2024 is a modest slip against that guided window.

events.headline: Senate Finance Committee proposes accelerating the phase-out of solar/wind tax credits to 2028; First Solar shares fall sharply
events.detail: The committee's draft of what became the One Big Beautiful Bill Act proposed phasing out solar and wind credits by 2028 (versus the IRA's original 2032 schedule), while extending credits for hydro, nuclear and geothermal to 2036.
events.source_quote: First Solar (FSLR) declined 9% in after-hours trading following the announcement.

source.title: Senate committee's changes to tax bill slam US solar stocks

events.headline: One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed, preserving solar's Section 45X credit phase-out schedule but adding new foreign-sourcing restrictions
events.detail: The Act terminated the 45X credit for wind components made after 2027 but retained the original phase-down timeline for solar components; it also added Foreign Entity of Concern material-assistance thresholds (50% in 2026, rising to 85% by 2030) that solar manufacturers must meet to keep claiming the credit.

source.title: "One Big Beautiful Bill Act" Brings Big Changes to Green Energy Tax Credits

horizon_notes.1: Over the year to 2023-03-02, First Solar's actual 2022 results came in weaker than even the guidance issued at the cutoff: full-year diluted EPS was a $0.41 loss versus the $0.00-$0.60 range guided on 2022-03-01, with management citing $73.1 million of production start-up expense [e1][e7]. Within the same window the Inflation Reduction Act was signed and the company committed roughly $2.3 billion of newly announced US capacity across Ohio and Alabama, while completing its planned Japan exit somewhat later than the first-half-2022 timing flagged at the cutoff [e2][e3][e4][e5]. 2023 guidance issued alongside the FY2022 results called for a rebound to $7.00-$8.00 EPS. Interpretation: the pre-cutoff packet's bull case (bookings, cash cushion) gave a reader grounds to treat the guidance cut as temporary, but nothing in the packet anticipated a full-year loss below even the cut guidance's low end, or that a single piece of legislation passed five months after the cutoff would reshape the entire calculus behind the 2022 guidance.
horizon_notes.3: By 2025-03-02, both catalysts flagged at the cutoff had materialized close to schedule -- the third Ohio facility in the guided first half of 2023, the first India facility about a quarter later than the guided second half of 2023 [e8][e9] -- and First Solar had continued adding IRA-incentivized US capacity. The dominant story by year three, however, was policy risk to the same 45X credits that had driven that expansion: a June 2025 Senate Finance Committee proposal to accelerate the credit phase-out to 2028 sent First Solar shares down sharply before the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed July 4, 2025, preserved the original solar phase-out schedule (unlike wind) while adding new foreign-sourcing eligibility rules [e10][e11]. Interpretation: the packet's unresolved question about 'pending, not-yet-enacted' domestic manufacturing incentives was resolved within the first year by the IRA's passage, but the packet had no way to signal that by year three the durability of that same incentive would itself become the central risk to the capacity First Solar had built in response to it.

aftermath.attribution_caveat: Price moves have many causes; the events here are what was public, not a proof of why the price moved.
gaps: This case's research used 14 WebSearch calls against a stated budget of 10; no WebFetch overage occurred (10 of 25 used). Flagging for transparency; all events below are still individually sourced.

The exact calendar date the third Ohio facility began Series 7 production (e8) is not stated in the primary 10-K source ('during 2023' only); 2023-03-31 is an approximation from a secondary summary, not independently confirmed by opening the underlying 10-Q operational text.
The Commerce Department AD/CVD circumvention determination (e6) was not fetched directly; its content is corroborated by three independent secondary summaries rather than the primary press release.

Direct US government sources for the IRA's exact signing date (congress.gov, energy.gov) were unreachable (403/404); the date is corroborated via First Solar's own contemporaneous press release rather than a government source.

No event captures First Solar's 2023-2024 full-year results in detail (e.g. FY2023 EPS realized vs. the $7.00-$8.00 2023 guidance); this was outside the case's 1-year horizon and researched only lightly.

scene_check.voice: Solar manufacturer guides 2022 earnings to as little as zero after earning $4.38 a share in 2021; plans to double capital spending on new US and India plants.

claims.text: 2022 EPS guided to $0.00 to $0.60 versus $4.38 earned in 2021
2022 capex of $850 million to $1.1 billion, about double 2021
17.5 GW of 2021 net bookings and a guided $1.1 to 1.35 billion year-end net cash

debrief_check.s1: Worse than the headline: full-year 2022 came in at a $0.41 loss per share, below even the $0.00 low end, with $73 million of plant start-up cost. Then 2023 guidance called for $7 to $8 [e1][e7].
debrief_check.s2: Happened on schedule: the third Ohio plant started in the first half of 2023 and the India plant about a quarter late. After the Inflation Reduction Act in August 2022 the company announced roughly $2.3 billion more US capacity [e2][e3][e5][e8][e9].
debrief_check.s3: The bookings and cash cushion were real, but the year's re-rating came from a law passed five months after the cutoff, which the packet flagged only as 'pending, not yet enacted'. The bull case was right for a reason it did not contain.

assumptions.text: The profit drop is a one-year cost of building capacity, not a margin problem.
The order book means demand will fill the new plants.
The proposed US manufacturing incentives will become law.
After a 38% fall the price already reflects the guidance cut.
Module pricing is under structural pressure and the cut will not be the last.

thesis_check.a1: Evidence: 2022 ended in a $0.41 loss per share, below even the guided low end, with $73 million of plant start-up cost; 2023 guidance then called for $7 to 8 of EPS [e1][e7]. For this assumption: supported in direction, though the one bad year was worse than guided. Unknown: how much of the 2023 rebound came from the company's own execution versus the new tax credit.
thesis_check.a2: Evidence: both plants started on or near schedule and the company announced roughly $2.3 billion more US capacity within the year [e3][e5][e8][e9]. For this assumption: supported; demand was never the constraint in the record. Unknown: how much of the later order book depended on the 2022 law rather than the 2021 bookings.
thesis_check.a3: Evidence: the Inflation Reduction Act was signed in August 2022, five months after the cutoff, with a production credit for US-made modules [e2]. For this assumption: it happened. Three years on, the same credits became the main risk when a phase-out was proposed and then partly preserved [e10][e11]. Unknown at the cutoff: timing, which no packet could give.
thesis_check.a4: Evidence: within the year the shares roughly tripled; see the result tiles [e1][e2][e3]. For this assumption: the price at the cutoff did not reflect the guidance cut so much as ignore what came next; whether it was cheap depended on a law, not on the cut. Unknown: what the stock would have done without the Act.
thesis_check.a5: Evidence: 2022 was indeed worse than guided [e7], but 2023 guidance rebounded sharply and the US tariff circumvention finding and the tax credit changed the pricing environment [e6][e2]. For this assumption: not supported over the year; the pressure was real but was overtaken by policy. Unknown: the counterfactual without those policy changes.

baseline.narrative: Your window ends before the first new development in this record. The starting guidance cut and expansion plan are not yet enough to show why profits fell or whether the new capacity will find demand.

checks.a1: Unresolved. The starting guidance alone cannot establish whether the loss is a one-year buildout cost or a more lasting margin problem.
checks.a2: Unresolved. A reported order book at the cutoff does not establish that demand will still be there once the new plants are running.
checks.a3: Unresolved. The manufacturing incentive was only proposed at the cutoff; this record cannot establish whether or when it will become law.
checks.a4: Unresolved. No share-price outcome is available at the cutoff to establish how much of the guidance cut the price already reflected.
checks.a5: Unresolved. This record does not establish whether the pricing pressure behind the cut is structural or a one-year squeeze.

updates.narrative: The first quarter's loss tracked the range already guided, and the company left its full-year outlook unchanged rather than cutting it again.

checks.a1: Partly supported. The first-quarter loss matched guidance already issued, which the company reiterated rather than cut further. One quarter does not distinguish a temporary buildout cost from a lasting margin problem.

updates.narrative: Five months after the cutoff, the incentive law the packet had flagged only as proposed was signed, creating a new production credit for US-made solar components.

checks.a3: Supported. The manufacturing incentive legislation was signed into law, creating a per-component production credit for US-made modules. This record does not establish how durable that credit will prove.
checks.a4: Unresolved. The incentive that reshaped the outlook was legislation passed after the cutoff, not information already available when the price was set. This record does not show how much of the guidance cut itself the entry price already reflected.

updates.narrative: In the three months after the new law, the company announced roughly $2.3 billion of further US capacity across two more facilities, citing the incentive directly and continuing the buildout begun before the cutoff.

checks.a2: Partly supported. The company committed to further US capacity, including a fourth facility, citing the new law, a sign management still expected demand to fill plants under construction. New commitments do not by themselves prove the order book was sufficient.

updates.narrative: In December, regulators found that competitors were routing Chinese-made panels through other Southeast Asian countries to avoid existing duties, though a waiver meant no immediate cash impact.

checks.a5: Partly supported. Regulators found competitors circumventing existing China duties through other countries, evidence the module-pricing environment stayed contested. A duty waiver until mid-2024 means this record does not show any near-term effect on prices.

updates.narrative: At the one-year mark, the full-year loss came in worse than even the guided low end, but the company guided 2023 to a sharp rebound to $7-8 of EPS.

checks.a1: Mixed. The full-year loss was worse than even the guided low end, with $73 million of start-up cost cited, but 2023 guidance points to $7-8 of EPS. This does not settle how much of the rebound reflects execution versus the new tax credit.
checks.a5: Not supported over the year. 2022 results were worse than guided despite real pricing pressure, but 2023 guidance rebounded sharply after the new law. This record does not show whether pricing pressure eased or was simply outweighed by policy.

updates.narrative: Over the following year, both new plants named in the packet's catalysts began production: the third US facility on the guided first-half-2023 schedule, the India facility several months behind its guided second-half-2023 target.

checks.a2: Supported. Both new plants in the packet's catalysts list began production, one on schedule and one several months late. This confirms the buildout was completed as planned; it does not show whether shipments matched the new capacity.

updates.narrative: By mid-2025, a Senate committee proposed accelerating the phase-out of the same manufacturing credits the expansion had relied on, and shares fell sharply on the news.

checks.a3: Unresolved. A Senate committee proposed accelerating the manufacturing credit's phase-out from 2032 to 2028, three years after the credit took effect, putting its durability in question. Whether the proposal becomes law is not yet known at this date.

updates.narrative: The bill that followed preserved the original phase-out schedule for solar manufacturing credits, unlike wind, while adding new foreign-sourcing rules manufacturers must meet to keep claiming them.

checks.a3: Partly supported. The signed law kept the original phase-out timeline for solar manufacturing credits intact, unlike wind, but added foreign-sourcing thresholds rising to 85% by 2030. This record does not establish whether First Solar's supply chain will meet those thresholds.
